newsitem.title: USA: Union Carbide raising prices, sees Q4 hurt.
newsitem.headline: Union Carbide raising prices, sees Q4 hurt.

text.p: Union Carbide Corp said Wednesday that due to escalating raw materials costs, it will raise prices effective January 1 for polyethylene and ethylene glycol, its largest volume products, as well as for many of its solvents, monomers and intermediates.
Union Carbide said the price increases would not prevent fourth quarter earnings being hurt by higher raw materials costs.
The company said it will raise polyethylene prices $0.05 per pound and will raise ethylene glycol prices by $70 per ton, following a $30 per ton increase since September.
It said soaring raw materials costs have significantly eroded its profit margins, especially in polyethylene and ethylene glycol.
In the fourth quarter, the cost of ethane, a major raw material, will likely average $0.08 per gallon above costs in the third quarter, $0.18 per gallon above year-earlier levels, it said.

Union Carbide said the impact of rising raw material and energy costs alone is likely to reduce fourth quarter earnings per share by at least $0.25 compared to the third quarter, when it reported earnings of $1.08 per share fully diluted.
About two-thirds of the impact will be recognized in the Basic Chemicals & Polymers segment, it said.

It said operating profit for its Specialties and Intermediates segment would also decline from the third quarter, primarily reflecting seasonal weakness as well as the segment's share of increased energy and raw material costs.
Union Carbide said the total impact on earnings of the Specialties and Intermediates segment decline could be as much as $0.25 per share compared to the third quarter.
A company spokesman told Reuters that the total impact of all costs on the whole company would reduce fourth quarter earnings per share by $0.42.
Specialties and Intermediates segment operating profit for the year would likely increase by three to five percent compared to 1995, instead of the targeted 10 percent, the company said.
Union Carbide said it was ahead of schedule for reaching its $637 million target of cost reductions by the year 2000.
